content.text: NONE ARE FOR USE IN CHILDREN <2YO
: sxs of allergic response (itching, urticaria), anaphylaxis
: sedation, cog dysfun, dry mouth, blurred vision
-    MOA: H1-receptor antagonist (1st-gen, cross BBB) -> block CNS his wakefulness -> sedation (+ anticholinergic)
-    1st-gen: also brompheniramine, chlorpheniramine, clemastine (cross BBB → sedation + antimuscarinic)

-    2nd-gen: cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine, desloratadine, levocetirizine (⍉cross BBB → less sedation + ⍉antimuscarinic); use: allergic rhinitis, conjunctivitis, urticaria, atopy, eczema, food + drug allergy, hay fever
-    Clin Use: allergy sx (runny nose, sneezing, itchy/watery eyes, throat itching) · common cold sx · insomnia (OTC sedative; may help initiate sleep; tolerance develops)

-    Caution: marked drowsiness (↑ w EToH/sedatives/tranquilizers) · ask doctor first: breathing problems, glaucoma, trouble urinating (enlrg prostate) · ⍉ use to make a child sleepy · excitability (children)
-    Toxicity: antimuscarinic + H1 block + Na-channel block → anticholinergic syndrome, sedation, seizure/dysrhythmia
- adults + children ≥12 y: 1-2 tabs (25 mg each)

: cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracell receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synth of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from musc/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits #/activity of cells involved in inflam response
Inhibits his release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/H2O retention, potassium loss
•Tx of allergic rxns: drug, serum, and transfusion rxns
: ↑appetite/wt gain, fluid retention, emotional instability, insomnia, indigestion, bitter taste, ↑BP/BG

: osteoporosis, GI (ulceration, bleed), psychiatric (mood, psychosis), cataracts, glaucoma, CV (HTN, edema, hypokalemia), diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Cushingoid syndrome, growth failure, impaired wound heal, adrenal suppression, IS
↑bone catabolism or antagonize vit D driven Ca absorb
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod -> take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal
: H2RAs; decrease gastric acid secretion by preventing his release from the enterochromaffin-like cells so it cannot stim parietal cells to release gastric acid
: H2RAs selectively and competitively inhibit the actions of his @ the H2 receptors
•IV doses: CNS effects – confusion, delirium, slurred speech, hallucination
Competitively inhibit his binding to H2 on gastric parietal cells
Gastric acid secretion: effect meal-stim secret & basal secret
SE:    -    HA           -    Dry Mouth         -    GI Sx: N/D, constipation
Renal dose adjust                    -    Hepatic dose adjust
MOA:  anti-androgen effects (more w ↑doses) -> gynecomastia, galactorrhea (cont. milk release), impotence, ↓libido
⍉recommended for use in pts <2yrs w/ renal or hepatic impairment
More drowsiness than loratadine, faster onset

roles.drugs: Bradykinin-mediated: stop the ACE inhibitor (resolves in ~24–48 h). Severe, progressing or refractory: C1 inhibitor concentrate, fresh frozen plasma, possibly ecallantide or icatibant. Epinephrine, steroids and antihistamines not shown to work
